sources.note: Nothing. Terebu occurs only in the Schouten/Kairiru subgroup listing; no sketch, no data.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. (sec. 5.2 The Schouten chain, pp. 120-132; App. A/B data sources)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988) (also lendable online at archive.org)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing on Terebu. Terebu appears only as a row in the Proto Schouten consonant/vowel correspondence tables and in cognate sets (data source 'Kaiep (Terebu) Laycock n.d.', App. B); p. 123: 'Kaiep and Terebu (related at dialect level)'. The only stress passage in the Schouten material is the Ali/Tumleo Verner's-law discussion at (3.115), p. 86, which does not concern Terebu.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1976. Austronesian languages: Sepik Provinces. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 399-418. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Survey and classification with comparative wordlist; Terebu named once (Kaiep speakers 'scattered throughout Terebu and Samap villages'); the phonological remarks (p. 404) concern stop voicing, palatalisation and loss of POC *k, no stress for any Sepik Austronesian language.

sources.note: Recorded word- and phrase-list of Kaiep, which Ross 1988 and Laycock 1973 treat as the same language as Terebu at dialect level; audio would allow stress placement to be heard directly. Not a statement.

sources.note: The only primary Terebu-language data in existence (source of Ross 1988's 'Kaiep (Terebu)' forms). Laycock's field wordlists elsewhere carry accent marks on forms (cf. his Bungain notebooks as reported by Kulick & Terrill 2019), so the Terebu list may show where he heard stress, even though it will contain no statement.
